mainEntity.name: How long does composite bonding last for white spot treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding for white spots typically lasts 5-10 years with proper care and maintenance. Longevity depends on factors including location, size of treatment area, oral hygiene, and dietary habits. Regular dental check-ups help monitor bonding integrity and identify any maintenance needs early.

mainEntity.name: Is composite bonding painful for treating white spots?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding for white spots is generally painless as the procedure typically requires minimal tooth preparation. Most patients experience no discomfort during treatment. Local anaesthesia is rarely needed unless deeper enamel preparation is required for optimal bonding.

mainEntity.name: Can white spots return after composite bonding treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: New white spots are unlikely to develop in areas covered by composite bonding, as the resin material sits over the original enamel. However, new white spots may develop on adjacent untreated tooth surfaces if underlying risk factors persist, and bonding may require maintenance or replacement over time. Maintaining good oral hygiene and regular dental care helps prevent new lesions.

mainEntity.name: Will composite bonding stain or discolour over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: High-quality composite materials used for bonding are resistant to staining but may gradually pick up surface stains from coffee, tea, or tobacco over several years. Professional polishing during routine dental visits can help maintain optimal appearance and extend treatment longevity.

mainEntity.name: How much does composite bonding cost for white spot treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding costs vary depending on the number of teeth treated, size of white spots, and complexity of the case. During consultation, your dentist can provide accurate cost estimates based on your specific treatment needs and aesthetic goals.

mainEntity.name: Can children have composite bonding for white spots?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite bonding may be suitable for children with permanent teeth, depending on their age, cooperation level, and specific clinical circumstances. Your dentist will assess whether treatment timing is appropriate or if waiting until tooth development is complete would be preferable.
